design:
Each weak visual was refined on the isolation bench first (`vision/isolation_v012.md`): the template forced alone into a picture, cut out with nothing else around it and read blind by a fresh reader, nine rounds and 42 cut-outs in all. The first round found the kick read as "walking ... and the ball is rolling past her foot" or a back-heel, the spade's blade as "a flat plate or spatula" that "could be read as hovering", the square wheel as "a square frame, a crate end or a window", the box just above the pickets as "resting or balanced at an angle on top of the fence", and the parked bicycle's stand as "too long and in an odd position". Each was redrawn and read again until it read as intended: the kick "mid-kick: she balances on one leg while the other leg swings out ... toward a small orange ball", the spade "digging a hole ... The shovel blade is in a dark hole and holds a clump of brown dirt", the box "floating or flying. Nothing holds it up", the square wheels "square, and wrong" with no crate, box, octagon or badly drawn round wheel in any of four readings.

Then the changes were read blind in whole test scenes among other events, five rounds and nineteen pictures, one reader each, with the screen's own prompt (`vision/design_tests_v012.md`). The scenes sent three visuals back to the bench: the spade blade still read as "a separate flat piece (like a plank or tray)", a long-legged kicker as "walking or stepping ... about to stumble" (her kicking foot was nearly on the ground: the foot is now raised in proportion to the leg), and the square wheel as "a crate" and later as "a round wheel drawn badly". In a busy park the swing arcs drawn up a child's raised leg read as "an untied shoelace", and now follow the foot's path about the hip. The scenes also added placement rules: the hole clear of standing structures (one dug at a clothesline post "suggests the post is about to be undermined"), the ground ahead of the kicked ball clear (a ball heading for the square-wheeled barrow), and the square-wheeled object wholly on or off the path (the path's edge seen through the open wheel drew a round wheel inside the square).
intro: All five templates that failed in v0.11 passed the ninth screen with full marks, each in every picture it appeared in: the kick ("one leg swung out kicking"), the digger ("digging with a shovel, looking down at the hole"), the play bow ("in a play bow with a yellow-green tennis ball by its nose"), the floating box ("in the sky above the fence, tilted at an angle; in mid-air") and the square wheel ("drawn as a square with spokes"). The gate rose from 59 to 63 of 64, the most of any screen, and the set scored its best action, inference and overall means of the nine screens with no item misread. One template fails, `blocked_hose`, by three half points (`vision/flaws_v012.md`).
screen: Across all 60 pictures only 8 of 694 scored items fell short of full marks (11 of 705 in v0.11), every one a half point: a reading offered as one of two ("stalking the red bird, but it could just be walking"; a goat "standing on or right next to the hose") or a visible motion given without its purpose (a duck "swimming toward the crumbs", never said to want them). Unintended oddities rose from 1.0 to 1.5 per picture. Three of the 32 are near-misses the readers raised and dismissed themselves, which earlier scorers mostly left out; most of the rest are mild ("slightly odd but plausible"). The real ones are on the v0.13 list: the floating box's shadow, now far below the raised box, read as a shadow "with nothing above it"; a kicked ball "may be heading for the child" in a sandbox; a throw arced toward the cat on the fence; sleeping pets lying flat "could also be read as collapsed".
redrawn: All five read with full marks in all three pictures each. None of the readings the isolation bench chased came back: no bat, no resting or unwell digger, no stretch, no box resting on the fence, no crate in front of the wheel.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (59 in three, 5 in four to six). The one failure, `blocked_hose`, passed in v0.10 and v0.11; here it lost two half points in one probe picture, where a goat stood "on or right next to the hose" and the stopped water was "one reading ... another: the water simply hasn't been turned on yet", and one in another, where a woman might be "just adjusting the nozzle". The retest of v0.9 put reader variance at about five templates between screens; a gate of 63 is the first to fall well inside it.
